design_gotchas.title: Silent Legacy (CSO: SFB) vs New Chip (CSO: RFAB) Die Split Under Identical OPN — Conflicting ESR Windows!
design_gotchas.detail: Rev K (Dec 2025, p.4 & p.31) reveals TPS76333DBVR (marking 'PBEI') ships with two distinct dies identifiable only on the reel label (CSO: SFB Legacy vs CSO: RFAB New). Legacy requires COUT >= 4.7 uF with 0.3–10 Ohm ESR (unstable on bare MLCCs), whereas New chip accepts 0–1 Ohm ESR (unstable above 1 Ohm!). Designs exposed to mixed inventory must constrain COUT >= 4.7 uF with 0.3–1.0 Ohm ESR.

design_gotchas.title: New Chip Ground Current (IQ) Jumps 9x Under Load (765 uA Typ / 1060 uA Max vs 85 uA Legacy)
design_gotchas.detail: While New chip lowers no-load IQ to 65 uA typ (p.7), its ground current jumps to 765 uA typ / 890 uA max at 25°C (1060 uA max over temp) for any load from 1 mA to 150 mA—nearly 9x higher than Legacy chip's flat 85 uA typ (140 uA max). Battery-powered meters or sensors idling at 1–5 mA lose substantial battery life after transitioning to RFAB lots.

design_gotchas.title: New Chip Brief Line-Transient Shutdown & Tighter EN Low Threshold (0.15 V vs 0.5 V)
design_gotchas.detail: Section 7.1.9 (p.25) warns that very large or fast VIN steps on the New chip can trigger a brief output shutdown lasting up to a few hundred microseconds unless slew rate stays below Figure 7-3. Furthermore, New chip lowers EN guaranteed-OFF threshold from 0.5 V down to 0.15 V (p.8)—noisy MCU GPIO lows at 0.3 V can fail to disable RFAB parts.

design_gotchas.title: No Reverse-Current Protection & 10 V Legacy Input/EN Ceiling
design_gotchas.detail: TPS76333DBVR lacks internal reverse-current blocking (Figure 7-2, p.23 recommends an external series diode on VIN when VOUT can exceed VIN). Do not rely on the New chip's 18 V abs max rating on VIN/EN unless incoming QA strictly gates reels to CSO: RFAB; Legacy SFB lots remain capped at 10 V VIN and VIN + 0.3 V on EN (p.4).

typical_use_cases: Legacy 5 V–10 V industrial, smoke detector, thermostat, and smart-meter 3.3 V / 150 mA LDO sockets requiring standard SOT-23-5 pinout
Medium-voltage (up to 10 V operating) battery pack and cordless tool auxiliary 3.3 V regulators
Pin-compatible migration target when auditing older tantalum-compensated SOT-23-5 LDOs against modern ceramic-stable alternatives like TPS7A2433DBVR
engineering_summary: The Texas Instruments TPS76333DBVR is a 2.7 V to 10 V input, 150 mA fixed 3.3 V LDO in a standard 5-pin DBV SOT-23-5 package (1=IN, 2=GND, 3=EN, 4=NC, 5=OUT). Revision K (Dec 2025) introduces a major split between Legacy (CSO: SFB) and New (CSO: RFAB) dies under the exact same OPN: New chip improves dropout (180 vs 300 mV typ), accuracy (±2.0% vs ±3.75%), and RθJA (178.6 vs 205.3 °C/W) and enables ceramic stability (0–1 Ohm ESR), but raises 1–150 mA ground current 9x to 765 uA typ (1060 uA max), drops EN-low to 0.15 V, and introduces a line-transient brief-shutdown boundary.

audit_notes: 300 DPI PNG Vision on p.3 confirmed Figure 4-1 DBV SOT-23-5 Top View pinout (1=IN, 2=GND, 3=EN, 4=NC on fixed TPS76333 / FB on adjustable TPS76301, 5=OUT).

300 DPI PNG Vision on p.4–5 confirmed Rev K (Dec 2025) Legacy vs New chip split: Abs Max VIN/EN (10 V / VIN+0.3 V legacy vs 18 V / 18 V new), COUT/ESR (4.7 uF & 0.3–10 Ohm legacy vs 1–220 uF & 0–1 Ohm new), and DBV RθJA (205.3 legacy vs 178.6 °C/W new).

300 DPI PNG Vision on p.7–9 confirmed TPS76333 accuracy (±2.0% new vs ±3.75% legacy), IQ (65 uA @ 0 mA / 765 uA typ @ 1–150 mA new vs 85 uA legacy), Vn (165 vs 140 uVRMS), ISTANDBY (1.12/2.75 uA new at EN<0.15 V vs 0.5/1 uA legacy at EN<0.5 V), PSRR (58 vs 60 dB @ 1 kHz), and VDO @ 150 mA (180 mV typ / 254 mV max new vs 300/500 mV legacy).

Path A verified Table 8-1 (p.31) CSO: SFB vs RFAB reel labeling, Sec. 7.1.9 (p.25) new-chip line-transient brief shutdown warning, Fig. 7-2 (p.23) reverse-current diode requirement, and Active Production OPN TPS76333DBVR (marking 'PBEI', p.34).
